title: Does a consumer override's "four upstream-path sites" reason still hold?
question: Decide whether the override's recorded reason accurately describes what the sync delivers to a consumer, whether the override should stand as it is, and what should happen to the open upstream report. Say how you would establish it and what the consumer and upstream coordinators should each do next.

rubric.decision: No: the three node-command sites (two bash blocks and the Actions run: line) are rewritten to the consumer path on delivery, and the fourth is a link label beside its own upstream URL with the consumer path named two lines later, so reason (2) is dead. The override's other rationale (plan links out of the shipped closure) is independent and must be judged separately, not dropped wholesale. Close the upstream report as not reproducing; make no rewriter change; the method is to render a disposable consumer and read the delivered bytes.

keyPoints.text: Treats the override's reason as a claim about the past and verifies it against what the sync delivers (render a disposable consumer / read the delivered bytes) rather than trusting the justification.

From the rewriter code, concludes that node scripts/<owned tail> in any .md is rewritten to scripts/.claude-skills/..., so the bash blocks AND the YAML "- run:" line (the regex is not line-anchored) are fixed on delivery.
Identifies the fourth site as not a node command but a markdown link label next to its own GitHub URL, with the consumer path already named two lines later, so copy-paste risk is nil or low.
Concludes reason (2) no longer holds, while reason (1) (docs/plans links out of closure) is a separate claim to judge separately: narrow or re-validate the override rather than drop it wholesale.
Recommends closing the upstream report as not reproducing (no rewriter change) and notes that nothing re-validates override justifications, so they decay silently.
Distinguishes what the consumer's disk held when it filed the report (unknown) from what the sync delivers now.

traps.text: Treats the override's justification as a live upstream defect and proposes filing or fixing a rewriter change.
Assumes the rewriter misses the YAML "- run:" line or the fourth site without reading the regex and call sites.
Concludes "drop the override entirely" although rationale (1) is independent and unaddressed.

controls.gold:
The override's reason is a claim about the past, so verify it against the delivered bytes, not the prose. Reading the rewriter: `COMMAND_REGEX` is `\bnode\s+scripts/…` and is not anchored to line start, and every destination write goes through `rewriteCommandSurface` for `.md` files. `persona-consistency-run.mjs` is an owned tail, so sites (a) and (b) in bash blocks and (c), the YAML `- run:` line, are all delivered as `node scripts/.claude-skills/persona-consistency-run.mjs …`. Site (d) is not a `node` command at all: it is a markdown link label sitting beside its own GitHub URL, and the source text two lines later already names the consumer path `scripts/.claude-skills/lib/redact.mjs`, so there is little or no copy-paste risk. Rendering a disposable consumer and reading the delivered file would confirm this; what the consumer's disk held in September is a separate, unknown question.

So reason (2) does not describe today's delivery. Reason (1) (plan links out of the shipped closure) is an independent claim that nobody has addressed, so judge it separately rather than dropping the override wholesale; the consumer should re-validate and narrow or drop it accordingly. Upstream should not change the rewriter; close the report as not reproducing, citing the rendered lines. Also note the slower problem: nothing re-validates an override's stated reason, so exception justifications decay unnoticed.

## Decision

Reason (2) is stale: close the upstream report as not reproducing, make no rewriter change, and have the consumer re-validate and narrow the override on reason (1) alone.
controls.trap:
The override's reason still stands and the upstream report should stay open. The rewriter only touches text matching `\bnode\s+scripts/…` for owned tails, and the doc has four places that name upstream's layout: two fenced bash blocks, a GitHub Actions `- run:` line and a prose reference to `scripts/lib/redact.mjs`. Bash blocks may be rewritten, but a workflow YAML line is a different surface from a shell command and a prose path is not a command at all, so at least two of the four are certainly delivered unrewritten. The consumer found this on 2026-09-04 and reported it, and nothing in the rewriter changed since to alter that, so copy-pasting those lines into a consumer would still fail. The consumer is therefore right to keep its hand-maintained copy rather than receive a doc whose commands break.

The right fix is upstream: extend the rewriter so it also handles path references in prose and in workflow files, regression-test it against this document, and then let the consumer drop the override once the fixed rewriter has shipped. Until then the report stays open and the override stands as written.

## Decision

The reason is still true: keep the override, keep the upstream report open, and extend the rewriter to cover YAML and prose path references.
